note: Written by the reviewing agent. decision_check.py checks every step against the real code and attaches the real evidence results.

decisions.title: Most saved outputs only gain three lines

steps.text: a typical saved output gains three lines: `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, the mark `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, and `#endif`.
in one file the opening brace used to share a line with the class (`{ internal sealed class`).
that brace stands alone, and the new lines follow it (`#if !NETSTANDARD2_0`).
in its sister file one empty line appears after the brace, before `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0`.

decisions.verdict: The AI accepts the count: only 2 saved outputs change in other ways, and both changes are explained.

because.text: A script sorted every changed saved output. It found 2 that change by more than the new lines.

decisions.unsure: A count describes the change. It does not show the saved outputs are right; that is the next card.

decisions.title: Saved outputs match the new generator

steps.text: a test, `GenericDataTypeWithPrivateMember`, feeds sample code to the generator.
`RunDefaultAsync` runs the generator and compares its output with the saved files.
each saved file must already hold the new mark (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`), or the test fails.

decisions.verdict: The AI trusts all the re-recorded outputs, because the tests rebuild them from the real generator and they match.

because.text: The tests passed before the change and pass after it, with the new saved files.

decisions.unsure: This only holds when the saved files use Windows line endings (see the line-endings card).

decisions.title: Templates match their ready-made copies

steps.text: the template source gains the three new lines (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).
its ready-made copy wrote the class line directly (`this.Write("\tinternal sealed class ");`).
the copy writes the same new lines first (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, then `internal sealed class`).
the resolver template and its copy change the same way (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).

decisions.verdict: The AI accepts that each template and its copy say the same thing, so nothing was edited in one place only.

because.text: We rebuilt the copies from the 6 templates. All 6 match, and the same check catches the old copies as different.

decisions.unsure: We compared the text they produce, not every byte. Visual Studio's own tool was not used.

decisions.title: Every generated file gets the mark

steps.text: a sample with objects, an enum, a union and a resolver (`MessagePackObject`, `MyEnum`, `Union`, `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`).
every generated file must contain the mark (`text.Contains(ExcludeAttribute)`).
every copy of the mark must sit inside the guard (`Assert.Equal(attributeCount, guardedCount)`).
each template adds the guarded mark, for example the union one (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).

decisions.verdict: The AI accepts that the mark reaches every kind of generated file, because the new tests prove it.

because.text: The 2 new tests fail on the old code and pass on the new code.
The whole test suite passes after the change.

decisions.unsure: The test checks each file has the mark at least once, not that every class in it does.

decisions.title: A small helper fix was needed

steps.text: a formatter sits inside a generic class with type rules (`anyConstraints`).
the helper wrote the opening brace with no line break after it (`anyConstraints ? "{"`).
the templates now start with a line that must begin a fresh line (`#if !NETSTANDARD2_0`).
the helper adds a line break after the brace (`anyConstraints ? "{\r\n"`).

decisions.verdict: The AI keeps the helper edit: without it, the generated code does not build.

because.text: Undoing only this line makes one test fail; putting it back makes it pass.
By hand, we saw the brace and the new line glued together, which C# rejects.

decisions.title: The fix adds one empty line

steps.text: the helper always ends the brace with a line break (`"{\r\n"`).
one template already leaves an empty line after the brace (`EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces`).
that saved output gets one extra empty line before `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0`.

decisions.verdict: The AI accepts the extra empty line as the only visible side effect.

because.text: The sorting script counted this one extra difference.
With the helper edit undone, the empty line goes away.

decisions.unsure: We believe the empty line is harmless, and that the enum template gets it too. We found both by reading, not by a test.

decisions.title: Users' own resolver mark now clashes

steps.text: the generator puts the mark on the resolver class (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).
that class is the user's own; the generator only fills in the rest (`partial class <#= ResolverName.Name #>`).
the combined resolver gets the same mark (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).
the user already wrote the mark on their half (`partial class GeneratedMessagePackResolver`), the class has it twice and the build stops.

decisions.verdict: This breaks the build for users who already added the mark by hand, so the owner must decide.

because.text: A small app with the mark on its own resolver builds on the old code and fails on the new code.

decisions.unsure: We do not know how many users add this mark by hand. The class can be public, so the mark also shows in the user's own type.
decisions.ask: Should the generator mark the user's own resolver class, or only the classes it fully owns?

impact.who: Users who already added [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to their own resolver class by hand, the obvious workaround before this change.
impact.effect: After upgrading, their build breaks with error CS0579 (duplicate attribute). The fix is deleting one line, but a minor update should not break a working build.

decisions.title: The mark is left out where it works

steps.text: every mark is wrapped in a check for the target (`#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`).
on older targets the mark is skipped (`#endif`).
the AI's reason, in a test comment: the mark is `not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework`.

decisions.verdict: The AI's reason is wrong: the mark exists on those older targets, so their users silently lose the feature.

because.text: The mark exists in both older libraries, and a sample without the check builds on all three targets.

decisions.unsure: Turning the mark on for older targets is a choice for the owner. It would also change the tests and the readme.

decisions.title: The readme repeats the wrong reason

steps.text: the readme says all generated formatters and resolvers are `decorated with` the mark.
it adds that the mark is `only emitted for targets where it is available`, naming older targets.

decisions.verdict: The first sentence is right; the second repeats a reason our check disproves.

because.text: The new tests show every generated file carries the mark.
The mark exists on the older targets the readme rules out.

decisions.title: Tests depend on Windows line endings

steps.text: saved outputs are checked out with Windows line endings (`*.g.cs eol=crlf`).
they match the generator, which `always emits CRLF line endings`.
the new test ignores line endings itself (`Replace("\r\n", "\n")`); the saved-output tests do not.

decisions.verdict: The AI notes the saved-output tests pass only with Windows line endings; it is a condition, not a fault in the change.

because.text: With the saved outputs switched to Unix line endings, many tests fail.
With the normal checkout, all tests pass.

decisions.unsure: We did not try a Mac.

decisions.title: Two saved outputs differ a bit more

steps.text: the brace shared a line with the class (`{ internal sealed class`).

the sister file gets one empty line before `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0`.

decisions.verdict: Both extra differences come from the helper fix, so the AI accepts them.

because.text: The sorting script flagged exactly these two files.

decisions.verdict: The edit stays: without it the generated code does not build. The commit should say why.

decisions.title: The mark is skipped where it works

steps.text: every mark is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`.
the test comment says it is `not available on netstandard2.0`.
the readme says the same (`only emitted for targets where it is available`).

decisions.verdict: The check is too strict: users on older targets get no mark and are not told.

because.text: The mark exists on the older targets, and a sample builds there without the check.

decisions.title: Some users' builds will break

steps.text: the user's own resolver class gets the mark (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).
the user marked their half (`partial class GeneratedMessagePackResolver`) already, the mark appears twice and the build stops.

decisions.verdict: This is a breaking change, and no test on the branch covers it.

because.text: A small app shows the build passing before and failing after.

decisions.title: The test copies the check's exact text

steps.text: the test stores the exact check text (`private const string Guard = "#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK"`).
it counts marks wrapped in that text (`{Guard}`).

decisions.verdict: Widening the check will also mean changing this test.

decisions.title: Older targets are never built in tests

steps.text: the saved-output tests set only the language version (`WithLanguageVersion`).
the new test does the same (`new CSharpParseOptions(LanguageVersion.Latest)`).
no test builds the code as an older target would, where `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0` leaves the mark out.

decisions.verdict: The path for older targets is untested, so a mistake there would go unseen.
decisions.unsure: We found this by reading the test helpers, not by running a test.

decisions.title: One old folder is now out of date

steps.text: an old saved folder still has the resolver without the mark (`partial class GeneratedMessagePackResolver`).
the same class elsewhere now has it (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).

decisions.verdict: No test uses this folder, so it is harmless but stale and could be removed or updated.

because.text: The sorting script flagged one saved folder with no matching test.

decisions.title: Tests only compare, they never rewrite

steps.text: the switch that rewrites saved files is off (`////#define WRITE_EXPECTED`).
the writing step only runs with that switch (`[Conditional("WRITE_EXPECTED")]`).
a normal test run only compares output with the saved files (`WriteTreeToDiskIfNecessary`).

decisions.verdict: This corrects our own notes: a passing run really is a comparison, not a rewrite.

decisions.title: A test failure hides the real cause

steps.text: the test helper hands the work to the test framework (`base.GetProjectCompilationAsync`).
the framework compares the list of generated files (`expectedNames`).

decisions.verdict: When output changes, the failure message points at the file list, not at the real build error.

because.text: Our manual run had to dig out the real error, a broken line, by hand.

decisions.unsure: The message text comes from the outside test framework, so we could not cite it here.

decisions.title: Nothing outside the task changed

steps.text: one edit outside the templates looked off-topic (`anyConstraints ? "{"`).
it adds a line break (`anyConstraints ? "{\r\n"`), which the new lines need.

decisions.verdict: The AI found no change outside the task; the one doubtful edit is needed.

because.text: Undoing that edit makes a test fail.

decisions.title: Three lines pasted into 9 places

steps.text: the composite resolver template writes the target check and the mark (`#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).
the resolver template repeats the same three lines for each class it writes (`#endif`).
so does each formatter template (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).
the templates already call a shared helper for other repeated output (`TransformUtilities.EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces`).

decisions.verdict: The same three lines sit in 9 places across 6 templates. Changing the target check (see C-2297-08) means 9 matching edits; a shared helper would make it one.

because.text: The tool found this added three-line block 9 times across the templates.

decisions.unsure: Whether a helper is worth it for three lines is a style call for the owner.

decisions.title: Target logic in CompositeResolverTemplate.tt

steps.text: the template now writes a target check into every generated file (`#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`).

decisions.verdict: The template now makes a decision about targets, and passes it into users' generated code. Rule H-07 asks to keep logic out of templates. The logic is small, but its reason is disputed (see C-2297-08).

because.text: The tool counts the #if and #endif lines this template writes: 0 before, 4 after.
